hints.title: Find one triangular end
hints.body: The cross-section is an equilateral triangle of side 2x. Splitting it in half gives a right triangle of hypotenuse 2x and base x.
hints.recap: A perpendicular cross-section can reduce solid geometry to a familiar triangle.
hints.pitfall: Half the base is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>; the full triangle base is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.pause: Use Pythagoras to find the height, then the triangular area.

recall.reminder: A perpendicular cross-section can reduce solid geometry to a familiar triangle.

hints.title: Build both measures from the faces
hints.body: The end area is 3x2. The volume is this area times d. The surface has two triangular ends and three rectangular faces, each with area 2xd.
hints.recap: A prism has volume equal to cross-sectional area times length; its surface includes all outer faces.
hints.pitfall: Do not omit either triangular end or count only one rectangular side.
hints.pause: Write formulas for the volume and total surface area.

recall.reminder: A prism has volume equal to cross-sectional area times length; its surface includes all outer faces.

hints.title: Equate and collect the length
hints.body: The stated numerical equality gives 3x2d=23x2+6xd. Move both terms containing d to one side and factor out d.
hints.recap: When a variable appears twice, collect it before dividing.
hints.pitfall: Lengths are positive: the denominator must permit <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
hints.pause: Solve for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow></math>, simplify, and select the matching expression.

recall.reminder: When a variable appears twice, collect it before dividing.

solution:
The triangular height is (2x)2−x2=3x, so the cross-sectional area is 12(2x)(3x)=3x2.

The volume is 3x2d. The total surface area is 23x2+3(2xd). Equating their numerical values gives d(3x2−6x)=23x2.

Since x>0, simplify to d=23x/(3x−6)=2x/(x−23): D. A positive length requires x>23; at the zero denominator the equality cannot hold.
knowledgePattern: Equate prism volume and total surface area numerically
